title: Human Development Index

blocks.heading: Human Development Index
blocks.text: HDI is a composite measure combining health, education and income dimensions of human development; it does not capture every aspect of development. Composite means that several components are brought together. This helps a comparison move beyond national income alone. A higher comparable HDI indicates a higher combined level of achievement in its included dimensions. It does not mean that each household has the same standard of living or that environmental and political conditions have been fully measured.

blocks.heading: Multidimensional Poverty Index
blocks.text: MPI is a measure of overlapping deprivations in health, education and living standards; it differs from an income-only poverty measure. Deprivation means a lack in a relevant condition, such as an essential service. The overlap matters: disadvantages can occur together in the same households. A lower comparable MPI indicates less multidimensional poverty. This is a different direction from HDI, where a higher value indicates higher achievement. Do not interpret a higher MPI as higher development simply because the number is larger.

blocks.heading: Read the two indices together
blocks.text: In an original fictional comparison made using consistent methods, Country M has HDI 0.72 and MPI 0.08; Country N has HDI 0.55 and MPI 0.24. M combines a higher HDI with a lower MPI. The HDI difference is 0.17 and MPI difference is 0.16. Together these support higher combined human development and less multidimensional poverty in M. Do not call either difference a percentage change or assume it tells how many people lack a service. The indices summarise different information and are not subtracted from each other. They help reveal why income alone is incomplete, but a national summary still needs more detailed evidence about particular groups.

blocks.heading: What the measures can guide
blocks.text: If two places have similar average incomes but different school participation and health conditions, the extra dimensions matter to a comparison of human development. If the question concerns households experiencing several disadvantages together, MPI addresses that issue more directly than an income average. Select a measure by the question it can answer. A local decision about a particular water point still needs local access and cost evidence; an index alone cannot locate the repair or establish its feasibility.

blocks.heading: Use dimensions, not a complicated formula
blocks.text: Health and education are developed in Topics 7.2 and 7.3. Here, explain what the indices represent, their directions and their limits. Calculating a full HDI or MPI from component data is outside this lesson's teaching depth.
